newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 12.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Despite requests from the EU, the Czech Republic will not cancel its new import deposit system, according to Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy, who was speaking for the cabinet.

- Czech Airlines (CSA) will probably not financially participate in the capital of Aero Vodochody, after the international consortium of Boeing, McDonnell Douglas and CSA won a public tender. CSA believes that nearly one billion crowns, which the consortium should invest to increase Aero's basic capital, will not be enough to save the company.

PRAVO - By the end of this year, Skoda Plzen will increase its current basic capital of 9.47 billion crowns by issuing new shares worth approximately 2.5 billion crowns. This was approved by shareholders during Friday's general meeting.
- The rating agency Standard & Poor's gave Ceska Exportni Banka a long-term credit rating of A. This is in connection with plans to issue five-year Eurobonds.
- Expenses for official media advertisements and outdoor advertisements last year reached 9.95 billion crowns, according to preliminary results from IP Praha.
- Demand for wine in the Czech Republic is currently 13 litres per capita yearly.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Worries about the economic and political situation in the country have led President Vaclav Havel to initiate a meeting with representatives of the cabinet coalition. Havel feels that the country is lacking long-term goals.
- According to material which Health Minister Jan Strasky gave to Education Minister Ivan Pilip at the end of last week, the number of beds at General Faculty Hospital should be reduced by one third.

- Japanese Nomura Bank, one of the two banks in the tender for 36 percent of IPB, announced its strategic intentions to offer IPB capital, financial know-how and human resources and to support the bank's management in reaching its goals.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said it is time for him to consider his presence in the cabinet if there will be discussions of solid restructuring within the cabinet. He does not want to leave his ministry immediately but at the end of the year.

- President Vaclav Havel said yesterday that among American senators and representatives there is enough intellectual oposition to expanding NATO. During his visit to the United States, which begins tomorrow, he will discuss NATO expansion not only with politicians, but also with the public.

- Tatra should obtain long-term cooperative contracts with Canadian Bombardier, Japanese Mitsubishi and German MTU and Schotte. Joint production should be for at least five years, giving Tatra a chance to expand its output.
- Last year's sales for ZAT Pribram were 343.4 million crowns, a year-on-year increase of 66.3 million crowns. ZAT is a manufacturer of driving systems for industrial application.

- Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said that the Czech economy is not in a crisis, but he admitted that it is at an important crossroads where mistakes from the past are appearing, belittling certain problems, primarily in legislative and supervisory areas.
